protagonist.who: You are a dungeon crawler standing in a single flooded reliquary chamber, holding a cursed talking sword that has already told you plainly where it was found and what it wants.
protagonist.wants: to get out of the reliquary alive with the sword still in your hand, because it is the only companion and weapon you have.
protagonist.can_do: move through the chamber, examine and use the sword and the reliquary's objects, talk with the sword, choose when to set it down or keep it, and let the sword cut, warn, or point.
protagonist.cannot_do: make the sword stop wanting to be returned, stop the return option from appearing, or survive the reliquary's hazards without the sword's help.

arena.description: A single flooded reliquary chamber, the whole dungeon reduced to one vaulted room with a return niche, a broken stair, and a sealed way out.

pressure.description: The reliquary is tightening around you: each time the sword's desire to be returned becomes an option, the chamber's hazards and wrong turns grow worse, and the return niche becomes easier to reach.
pressure.clock_or_stock: none tracked; the escalation is told through hazards and wrong turns, because 3-0c licenses only hazard_or_wrong_turn

opposition.who_or_what: the cursed talking sword, funny and menacing, the only companion in the reliquary
opposition.wants: to be put back where it was found.
opposition.means: it can talk, nudge, warn, refuse, point at the return niche, and let the reliquary's hazards worsen when its desire is ignored; it cannot make you set it down or make you keep it.

mediation.question: Does the sword stay with you as a companion, or go back to where it belongs?

to_reach_pole_a.pole: companionship: keep the sword in hand
to_reach_pole_a.what_you_must_do: use the sword in the reliquary, let it cut, warn, and point, and at a return opportunity refuse to set it down, even when the chamber makes the return easier to reach.
to_reach_pole_a.cost: the reliquary's hazards worsen, the sword's insistence becomes more menacing, and you lose the chance for restoration.

to_reach_pole_b.what_you_must_do: find the return niche, make the sword willing to be set down, and leave it there, even though that means surviving the reliquary without your companion and weapon.
to_reach_pole_b.cost: you lose the sword's company and help, and the bond is broken or left hollow.

levers: the return niche where the sword was found
the sword's stated desire, repeated as an option
the reliquary's hazard routes and wrong turns
a moment when the sword's curse takes your hand and points at the return niche

turns.situation: The flooded reliquary floor hides a route to the broken stair, and the cursed sword points first at the return niche, then at a wrong turn.
turns.what_you_must_do: find a safe route to the broken stair before the water finds the wrong turn

ways_through.way: you find the route, because you let the cursed sword warn you and keep it in hand
ways_through.cost: the water rises a hand's breadth, and the sword's pointing does not stop

ways_through.way: you find the route, because you examine the carved guide on the reliquary wall and ignore the sword's first warning
ways_through.cost: a wrong turn opens under your feet, and the sword's voice goes flat with menace

turns.situation: The sealed way out will not open until its flooded latch is cut or pried, and the cursed sword says it will help only if the return niche is promised.
turns.what_you_must_do: get the sealed way out open

ways_through.way: you get it open, because you promise the cursed sword the return niche and let it cut the latch
ways_through.cost: the promise hangs in the water, and the niche becomes the easiest place in the chamber to reach

ways_through.way: you get it open, because you pry the latch with the broken stair's iron while the cursed sword refuses to cut
ways_through.cost: the sword's warning is lost, and the stair's wrong turn is left unmarked

turns.situation: The cursed sword's curse takes your hand and points it at the return niche, and the water uses the moment to move.
turns.what_you_must_do: get your hand back before the water takes the niche

ways_through.way: you get your hand back, because you let the cursed sword finish pointing and then step past it
ways_through.cost: the sword knows you will not set it down, and its warning turns to menace

ways_through.way: you get your hand back, because you set the cursed sword in the return niche while your hand is still pointing
ways_through.cost: your hand is empty for the last step, and the sword's voice is farther away

turns.situation: The sealed way out is open, but the water is closing the chamber, and the cursed sword's desire to be returned is the last thing it says.
turns.what_you_must_do: get out of the reliquary before the water seals the stair

ways_through.way: you get out, because you set the cursed sword in the return niche and let it calm the water
ways_through.cost: you leave alone, and the niche keeps the last of its voice

ways_through.way: you get out, because you keep the cursed sword in hand and let it point the dry step
ways_through.cost: the water follows you to the threshold, and the sword's pointing hand does not let go

complications.description: The water drains toward the return niche as the sealed way out opens, making the niche the easiest place to stand and the hardest to leave.
The broken stair's iron latch is the only object the cursed sword will cut, and it is already wet with your pack's water.
A wrong turn in the flooded floor leads to a dry alcove that is only the return niche's shadow, and the cursed sword laughs at you for almost mistaking it.

cast_seeds.wants: to be put back where it was found
cast_seeds.holds: the knowledge of the return niche and the ability to influence the reliquary's hazards and the protagonist's hand
